\section{Assembly: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is an abelian variety}
\label{sec:pic0_isAbelianVariety}

A \(k\)-group scheme is an \emph{abelian variety} iff its underlying
\(k\)-scheme is a complete (proper) connected group variety
(Milne~\S I.1, p.~8). Combining the smoothness, properness, and
geometric irreducibility statements of this chapter with the
identity-component group-scheme structure of
\cref{chap:Picard_IdentityComponent} packages \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) as an
abelian variety of dimension \(g\). This is the load-bearing A.3.vii
gate for Route~A.

\begin{theorem}[\(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is an abelian variety]\leanok

        thm:pic0_geom_irred,
        thm:identity_component_is_subgroup_homomorphism}

  % \S I.1, p.~8 (definition of abelian variety) (read from
  % references/abelian-varieties.pdf, PDF p.~14).
  % SOURCE QUOTE:
  % "A complete connected group variety is called an abelian variety. As we
  % shall see, they are projective, and (fortunately) commutative. Their
  % group laws will be written additively. Thus \(t_a\) is now denoted

  % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 5, Rmk.~rmk:Jac;

  % Exercise~\ref{ex:jac}."
  \textit{Source: [Milne], ``Abelian Varieties'' (course notes, 2008),
  \S I.1, p.~8 (definition of abelian variety); [Kleiman], ``The
  Picard scheme'', \S 5, Rmk.~5.26 (the Jacobian
  \(J := \Pic^0_{X/S}\) of a smooth proper family of curves is a
  projective abelian \(S\)-scheme).}
  Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve of
  genus \(g\) over a field \(k\). The identity component
  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) (\cref{def:pic_zero_subscheme}) is an
  \emph{abelian variety over \(k\)} of dimension \(g\): the underlying
  \(k\)-scheme is smooth (\cref{thm:pic0_smooth}), proper

  (\cref{thm:identity_component_is_subgroup_homomorphism}). In
  particular, \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is automatically commutative (Milne~\S
  I.1, Cor.~1.4).
\end{theorem}

218	\section{The FGA representability theorem}
219	\label{sec:fga_pic_representability}
220	
221	We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck's existence theorem
222	for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian:
223	\(S = \Spec k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral
224	curve. The general theorem (Kleiman \S 4, Thm.~4.8) covers any
225	\(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric
226	fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise.
227	
228	\begin{theorem}[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]\leanok
229	  \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}
230	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.representable}
231	  \uses{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence, lem:smooth_proper_quotient,
232	        thm:quot_representable, def:rel_pic_sharp, def:has_rational_point,
233	        cor:flattening_stratification_curve, def:pic_sharp_representable,
234	        def:inst_pic_sharp_representable, lem:cech_flat_base_change}
235	  % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~th:main,
236	  % and Cor.~cor:algsch (specialisation to \(S = \Spec k\), \(X\) complete);
237	  % arXiv:math/0504020, pp.~26, 35 (read from
238	  % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex, L2155-L2166 + L2686-L2690).
239	  % Source identifiers: \begin{thm}\label{th:main}\end{thm}
240	  % and \begin{sbscor}\label{cor:algsch}\end{sbscor}.
241	  \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~4.8
242	  + Cor.~4.18.3.}
243	  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
244	  over \(k\) \emph{with a \(k\)-rational point}
245	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}). Then the relative Picard functor
246	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp} --- which under the
247	  rational-point hypothesis coincides with its \'etale sheafification
248	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), by Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 --- is representable by a
249	  \(k\)-scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over
250	  \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
251	  \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
252	  subschemes. The scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) is called the \emph{Picard scheme}
253	  of \(C/k\).
254	\end{theorem}
255	
256	\begin{proof}
257	  
258	  We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
259	  \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
260	  comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of
261	  \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme} and the relative Picard functor of
262	  \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
263	  correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.
264	
265	  \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
266	  By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
267	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}
268	  \mathcal O_{C \times_k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology
269	  and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of
270	  \(C\times_k T/T\)), the comparison map
271	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) \to \Pic_{(C/k)\et}(T)\) is bijective for all
272	  \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the \'etale sheaf
273	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which is what Kleiman's theorem produces; the same
274	  scheme then represents \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
275	
276	  \emph{Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.}
277	  For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq
278	  \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) be the \'etale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are
279	  represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) with
280	  \(\chi(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the
281	  Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation
282	  \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi\) form a
283	  disjoint open cover of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (openness via Kleiman's
284	  flat-base-change argument, \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change} / Stacks Tag 02KH;
285	  cf.\ EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to
286	  represent each \(P^\phi\) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective
287	  \(k\)-schemes.
288	
289	  \emph{Step 2: bound twists by \(m\)-regularity.}
290	  Given \(\phi\), fix \(m\) large enough that the \(T\)-points of \(P^\phi\) are
291	  representable by \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) satisfying
292	  \(R^i \pi_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0\) for all \(i \ge 1\), \(n \ge m\). Twisting
293	  by \(\mathcal{O}_C(m)\) defines an automorphism of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
294	  that carries \(P^\phi\) to \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) for \(\phi_0(n) := \phi(m + n)\).
295	  Hence it suffices to represent each \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) by a quasi-projective
296	  \(k\)-scheme.
297	
298	  \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}
299	  Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
300	  of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
301	  is representable by an open subscheme of \(\Hilb_{C/k}\) (and hence by an
302	  open subscheme of the Quot scheme of \cref{thm:quot_representable}), and
303	  is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along
304	  \(P^{\phi_0}_0 \hookrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) yields an open
305	  subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi_0}_0 \times_{\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
306	  of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection
307	  \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi_0}_0\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves:
308	  given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda\) of \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) represented by an \'etale
309	  cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times_k
310	  T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle
311	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to
312	  \(\mathcal{Q} := \pi_{T'*}\mathcal{L}'\) is smooth over \(T'\); an \'etale
313	  cover \(T_1 \to T'\) admits a \(T'\)-map \(T_1 \to \mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q})\)
314	  (EGA IV 17.16.3 (ii)) whose composition with the universal divisor map
315	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to Z\) produces the required \(T_1\)-point of \(Z\).
316	  Moreover, the first projection \(Z \times_{P^{\phi_0}_0} Z \to Z\) is
317	  smooth and proper.
318	
319	  \emph{Step 4: descend by the smooth-proper quotient lemma.}
320	  Apply Kleiman~\S 4, Lem.~4.9: given a surjection \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
321	  of \'etale sheaves with \(Z\) quasi-projective, \(R := Z \times_P Z\)
322	  representable, and the first projection \(R \to Z\) smooth and proper,
323	  \(P\) is representable by a quasi-projective scheme. In our case
324	  \(P = P^{\phi_0}_0\), \(Z\) and \(R\) as above, so \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) is
325	  quasi-projective. Reassembling over \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\) and
326	  over \(m\), the disjoint union of representable \(P^\phi\) pieces represents
327	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\). The total scheme is separated (as a disjoint
328	  union of separated quasi-projectives) and locally of finite type. This
329	  is Kleiman~\S 4, Cor.~4.18.3 in the \(S = \Spec k\),
330	  \(X = C\) complete case.
331	\end{proof}
332	
333	\subsection{The smooth-proper quotient lemma}
334	\label{subsec:fga_pic_qt}
335	
336	The structural lemma underlying step 4 above is recorded separately

Wire the headline to the infrastructure, and publish the true axiom frontier.

===== AJC.picrep | pending | Picard scheme representability cone
Represent the relative Picard functor by the Milne-Kollar route selected in informal/pic-representability-campaign.md: build Pic^r over a separably closed field from the h0=1 loci cut out by a tuple of rational points, glue, descend to k by a finite Galois quotient, then assemble the degrees by a coproduct. Completed inputs: line-bundle coherence, the Grassmannian and graded algebra substrate, glue-descent, Speiser semilinear descent, the affine Galois quotient, and the stable affine cover. Open inputs on this route: the rigidified pushforward gate (AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward, held by task ajc-gate), uniform H1 vanishing and the chi-ledger (AJC.rr, held by ajc-rr), Div^d representability, the Milne glue, and Galois descent of rigidified classes.

The Quot endgame is NOT this route. AJC.picrep.quot and AJC.picrep.serre describe it; the Lean tree marks HasSmoothProperQuotient permanently off-path because Altman-Kleiman descent needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not expressible at the pinned revision and without which the lemma is false (Hironaka free Z/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective threefold). Those nodes are retained, not revived: their divisor, Hilbert-scheme and Grassmannian substrate is consumed by the committed route, and only QuotRepresentability.lean and SerreFiniteness.lean are exclusive to the abandoned endgame.

Complete and sorry-free: Grassmannian representability, section graded rings and modules, Hilbert-Serre algebra, cell charts, and glue descent. The Nitsure Quot representability theorem remains under `AJC.picrep.quot`.

===== AJC.picrep.assembly | pending | Assemble the Picard scheme
Assemble the Picard scheme on the committed Milne-Kollar route: glue the h0=1 loci into Pic^r over a separably closed field (needs the 01JJ engine and a universe bridge, since picSharp is Type (u+1)-valued), spread the finite glue datum to a finite Galois level, descend picSharp points through rigidified pairs, and assemble the degree pieces as a coproduct over Z. ===== AJC.picrep.quot | pending | Nitsure Quot representability
OFF-PATH, retained not revived. Under projectivity, relative very ampleness and coherence, representability of the Quot functor from boundedness, the Grassmannian embedding, flattening stratification and closedness (Nitsure section 5). One open leaf: QuotRepresentability.lean:79.

===== AJC.picrep.quotbasechange | done | Quot base change and support
Sorry-free. Flat base change for the Quot construction and base change of the support of a quotient; these are the inputs the Nitsure representability endgame consumes. Modules: Picard/QuotFlatBaseChange, Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange, and the quasi-coherent descent machinery of Picard/QuotScheme.

===== AJC.picrep.rational-point | blocked | DECISION: the rational-point hypothesis
Needs a human decision. references/challenge.lean declares Jacobian C with no rational-point binder, but instHasPicScheme (Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316) makes [HasRationalPoint C] an essential hypothesis -- correctly so, since without a section Pic(C x_k T)/pi_T^* Pic(T) need not be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman's theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed to be a platform limitation, but mathlib v4.31 does have the etale topology (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50), so it is a design choice. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept a theorem strictly weaker than the challenge statement. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until it is settled.

===== AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward | active | Rigidified pushforward engine (gate factored into four named leaves)
GATE FACTORED (run 0053). HasRigidPushforward is now four exactly-stated leaves that are machine-checked to compose: Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean, hasRigidPushforward_of_leaves. (1) IsIntegral (P^1_k) -- integrality of the projective line over the ONE field k; this alone discharges the whole Serre-finiteness anchor hH0 at every finitely generated k-algebra A (Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Constants.lean, p1Cech_h0_fg_of_isIntegral), replacing the previous A-indexed family of anchors. GeometricallyIntegral is also plumbed and is strictly stronger; it reduces further to the integral model Proj Z[X0,X1]. (2) P1CechFibrewiseBridge -- fibrewise Cech H1-vanishing at scheme points implies d tensor kappa(m) surjective at maximal ideals. (3) P1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge -- the engine module conclusion implies p_*M locally free of rank fiberH0. (4) RigidPushforwardBaseChange -- the second gate field, zero infrastructure: every IsIso result for the adjoint mate in this tree needs [IsAffineHom f] and q is proper, so the entire content of the field is the non-affine case, and there is no composition/pasting API for pushforwardBaseChangeMap. CORRECTIONS: HasFiniteMapToP1 is NOT an open gate (it synthesizes for an AJC curve, sorry-free, clean axioms); and HasRigidPushforward has ZERO consumers anywhere in the workspace, so it is a prerequisite for future DivFamily work rather than a live blocker.

Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange (Picard/RigidPushforward.lean:342) is the second field of HasRigidPushforward and has NO infrastructure. Established by recon plus an adversarial re-verification: the tree's only IsIso theorems for the adjoint mate pushforwardBaseChangeMap are isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback (Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean:1108) and its chart form (:949), both requiring [IsAffineHom f] [IsAffineHom f']; with IsAffineHom q assumed the gate field closes in ONE line (probe-verified: the pinned pullback.condition is defeq to IsPullback.of_hasPullback's h.w, IsAffineHom f' follows by base-change stability, and the only residual obligation L.IsQuasicoherent comes from hL.isFinitePresentation). So the entire content of the field is the non-affine case for q : C_A -> Spec A. Two further obstacles: (a) there is NO composition/pasting API for pushforwardBaseChangeMap anywhere (no _comp, no pasting-of-squares lemma), so the natural route 'reduce along the finite affine pi_A : C_A -> P^1_A, then handle p : P^1_A -> Spec A' cannot be assembled even once the second half exists; (b) the only non-affine base-change iso in the tree, canonicalBaseChangeMap_isIso (Picard/QuotScheme.lean:6104), is about a DIFFERENT mate (built from the pullback 2-iso, not the unit; probe-verified not defeq) and assumes [Flat g], which this statement explicitly refuses. Cohomology/FlatBaseChange.lean:689 records the mate vs cancelBaseChange coherence as a known unresolved wall. The module-level input IS available: kerBaseChange bijective for EVERY base algebra, the fourth conclusion of p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing. Missing is the sheaf-level bridge, estimated 4-5 new bricks.

===== AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward.p1integral | pending | IsIntegral P^1_k -- the last H0-finiteness leaf
The whole B3 H0 anchor (finite generation of the Cech H0 of a finitely presented module on P^1_A, classically Serre finiteness) now rests on one statement: IsIntegral (P^1_k), integrality of the projective line over the single field k. The project has the surjectivity/spanning half only (span_p1CoordAway_pow_top, RiemannRoch/Adelic/P1ChartData.lean:265); RelLaurentChartData supplies spanning, never a basis, so any 'x-degree' argument is unsound without it. Write it Away.mk-first in the style of P1ChartData.lean:184-265 to dodge the val_injective isDefEq blowup. Landing the chart iso also yields IsReduced and IrreducibleSpace of P^1 by transport from mathlib's affine-space instances.

===== AJC.picrep.serre | pending | Serre finiteness and Hilbert polynomial
OFF-PATH, retained not revived. Finite generation of the section graded module plus the fibrewise graded Hilbert function; the two open leaves in SerreFiniteness.lean.

Needed by the Quot endgame (AJC.picrep.quot), not by the committed Milne-Kollar route, whose uniform-H1 input comes from cluster P instead (AJC.rr, task ajc-rr).
